eval_rubric:
1. Exactly 9 slides, same order as prior-deck.pptx, no slides added, removed, merged, or reordered. Titles/subjects, in order: Slide 1 "What makes a place a place to visit? Understanding peripheral tourism destinations in the making" (33rd Nordic Symposium on Tourism and Hospitality Research, Bornholm, 17-19 September 2025, presenter Viktor Smith and contributors Maximilian Block, Nicole Carpentari, Carsten Jacob Humlebaek); Slide 2 "Research context"; Slide 3 "Aim of this presentation"; Slide 4 "The 'below zero' scenario"; Slide 5 "What's in a (place) name?"; Slide 6 "Semiotic landscapes"; Slide 7 "A case study: Naming, framing, and finding 'Campina de Faro'"; Slide 8 "A few selected highlights"; Slide 9 "Next steps".
2. Slides 2-4 content carried forward without rewriting, summarizing away, or dropping specifics: the Horizon 2020 Innovation Action (2021-2024, 10 pilot cases) and the Horizon Europe project (2024-2027, 8 pilot cases) with the CBS team's cross-pilot-synergy role (slide 2); the conceptualizing aim across INCULTUM and SECreTour pilot cases and the "below zero" scenario quote ("we are not starting from zero -- we are still below zero") (slide 3); the four key traits of the below-zero scenario -- not yet recognized as touristic, local actors not yet identified/organized, limited or absent baseline data, and few financial resources requiring self-funding (slide 4).
3. Slides 5-7 content carried forward without rewriting, summarizing away, or dropping specifics: the four-perspective naming framework -- having a name for it, name-intrinsic cues ("Joyce Principle"), name-extrinsic cues ("Juliet Principle"), and larger sets of names shaping a wider topic (slide 5); the semiotic-landscape definition as the totality of communicative cues (verbal, visual, auditive, olfactory) shaping a person's understanding of a place (slide 6); Campina de Faro as a coastal plain in the Algarve hinterland (between Faro, Olhao, Loule), rich in heritage but unknown to the ~5 million yearly Algarve tourists, and the methodology -- a visitor survey (N=92) and in-depth interviews with residents/tourism professionals (N=15) (slide 7).
4. Slides 8-9 content carried forward without rewriting, summarizing away, or dropping specifics: the Perspective 1 finding that 85 of 92 (92.4%) nearby visitors and 4 of 7 in-depth-interviewed residents were unfamiliar with the name, and the Perspective 2 finding of mixed name-guessing ("area around Faro" vs. "a campsite"/"an airport") plus "campina" as an ordinary Portuguese word for farmland supplying a city (slide 8); the "next steps" typology of below-zero scenarios along other dimensions, closing with "For now: Any question?" (slide 9).
